title: Time to Cross a Bridge
statement:
`n` boxes sit in a warehouse on the right bank of a river, and `k` workers must carry all of them to a warehouse on the left bank. A single bridge joins the banks, and every worker starts on the left bank. Worker `i` is described by `time[i] = [right_i, pick_i, left_i, put_i]`: walking over the bridge to the right bank takes `right_i` minutes, taking a box out of the right warehouse takes `pick_i`, walking back over to the left bank with it takes `left_i`, and storing it in the left warehouse takes `put_i`. A worker carries one box per round trip and may make several round trips.

Worker `i` is **less efficient** than worker `j` when `left_i + right_i > left_j + right_j`, or when those two sums are equal and `i > j`. The bridge is shared by these rules:

- The bridge holds a single worker at once. Picking and putting happen off the bridge, and any number of workers may do them at the same time.
- Whenever the bridge is free, the workers holding a box and waiting on the right bank go first, the least efficient of them first. Only if nobody waits there does a worker waiting on the left bank start across, again the least efficient first. A worker who finishes picking or putting at the very minute the bridge becomes free is already waiting.
- Each trip to the right fetches one box, so once `n` workers in total have been sent across from the left bank, nobody else is sent.

Return the minute at which the last box arrives on the left bank, which is when the final right-to-left crossing ends (the time to store that box is not counted).
signature: int findCrossingTime(int n, int k, int[][] time)
notes:
## Intuition

This is a simulation, and the only hard part is answering "who goes next?" quickly. At any moment each worker is in one of four places: waiting on the left, waiting on the right with a box, busy picking on the right, or busy putting on the left. The waiting groups are asked "who is least efficient?", and the busy groups are asked "who finishes soonest?". Four priority queues answer both questions in O(log k), and the clock `now` only ever jumps to the next moment something can happen, so no minute-by-minute loop is needed.

## Approach

1. Put every worker in `leftWait`, a heap ordered by `slower` (bigger `right + left`, then bigger index). `rightWait` uses the same order; `leftBusy` and `rightBusy` hold `[finishTime, worker]` ordered by `sooner`. Set `remaining = n`, the boxes nobody has been sent for yet.
2. Each round, move everyone whose picking or putting has finished by `now` into the matching waiting heap.
3. If someone waits on the right, the least efficient one crosses left: add their `left` time to `now`. If no boxes remain unclaimed and nobody else is on the right bank, this was the last box: return `now`. Otherwise they start putting until `now + put`.
4. Else, if `remaining > 0` and someone waits on the left, the least efficient one crosses right, claims a box (`remaining--`) and starts picking until `now + pick`.
5. Else the bridge idles: jump `now` to the earliest finish time that matters (`leftBusy` only while boxes remain).

## Example 1, step by step

Crossing sums are 3, 4 and 5, so worker 2 is the least efficient. At `now = 0` worker 2 crosses right (`now = 1`, `remaining = 0`) and picks until 2. Nobody waits, so `now` jumps to 2; worker 2 crosses left in 4 minutes, `now = 6`. No box remains and the right bank is empty, so the answer is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O((n + k) log k): each box causes two crossings and two heap moves, and each idle jump is followed by a crossing.
- Space: O(k) for the four heaps.

## Pitfalls

- "Least efficient" goes first: the **largest** `right + left`, and on a tie the **largest** index.
- Release workers whose task ends exactly at `now` before choosing who crosses.
- Count boxes when a worker is sent right, not when one arrives back; otherwise extra workers cross for boxes that are already claimed.
- The answer is the arrival of the last box, not the end of its putting time.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `leftWait`, `rightWait` | workers waiting at each end of the bridge, least efficient on top |
| `leftBusy`, `rightBusy` | `[finishTime, worker]` for workers putting (left) or picking (right) |
| `cost` | each worker's crossing sum `right + left` |
| `now` | the current minute |
| `remaining` | boxes no worker has been sent for yet |
| `worker` | the worker who just took the bridge |
| `next` | the next minute at which a busy worker becomes free |
